effect_pct_measures: Generation speed, 16-bit to 4-bit build of Llama 3.1 8B
effect: 16-bit to 4-bit (Q4_K_M): size 14.96 -> 4.58 GiB (-69%), generation 29.2 -> 71.9 tok/s (+147%). 16-bit to 8-bit: -47% size, +75% speed. Quality kept: 96% to 101% at 8-bit and 4-bit
source: llama.cpp quantize README; "Give Me BF16 or Give Me Death"?

effect_pct_measures: Generation speed, MoE with 3B active against a dense 27B (2x to 3x, LLMeter's arithmetic)
options: Dense model, or MoE with few active parameters (for example 30B with 3B active)
what_it_changes: Speed at similar memory; quality differs by model
effect: On one MacBook Pro M5 Pro at 4-bit: MoE models with 3B active ran at 32 to 48 tok/s, the dense 27B at 16 tok/s (2x to 3x)

effect_pct_measures: AIME 2024 score, 1.5B distill 28.9 to full model 79.8 (LLMeter's arithmetic)
options: Smaller or larger model of one family, including distilled versions
effect: DeepSeek-R1 distills on AIME 2024: 1.5B 28.9, 7B 55.5, 14B 69.7, 32B 72.6, full model 79.8

effect_pct_measures: AIME 2024 score with reasoning, for a model trained for it; -24% to -64% on two small local models
options: Off, on, or low to maximum effort
what_it_changes: Quality on hard tasks; tokens and time
effect: Gains up to +104% on hard math for a model trained for it. On two small local models under fixed limits: score -24% to -64%, 6x to 8x the tokens, 8x to 9x the time
source: DeepSeek-R1 model card; LLMeter local runs

effect_pct_measures: Generation speed in the original paper (2x to 3x, LLMeter's arithmetic)
options: Off, or a small model of the same family as draft
effect: 2x to 3x in the original paper; not yet measured by LLMeter

effect_pct_measures: Perplexity loss at 4-bit with QAT, against a plain 4-bit build
options: Plain post-training quantization, calibrated (importance matrix, GPTQ, AWQ), or quantization-aware training (QAT) by the developer
effect: QAT: 54% less perplexity loss at 4-bit, same memory as any 4-bit build (Gemma 3 27B: 54 GB -> 14.1 GB)

effect_pct_measures: Speed of each request with 4 in flight
what_it_changes: Total throughput against speed of each request; memory
effect: Qwen3.8 27B: 16.7 -> 11.1 tok/s per request at 4 in flight (-34%); Nanbeige4.3 33B: 13.6 -> 6.9 (-49%). Each slot adds KV cache memory

effect_pct_measures: Time to first token with a cached prefix
options: Keep a repeated prefix cached (default in most local runtimes; a priced option in cloud APIs)
effect: -31% to -79% time to first token; cached input at 10% of the normal price

effect_pct_measures: SWE-bench Lite resolved, same model, plain shell agent to SWE-agent
options: Chat window, plain shell agent, or a coding agent with purpose-built tools
effect: +64% on SWE-bench Lite for the same model (11.0 -> 18.0)

effect_pct_measures: Generation speed gap between two runtimes on the same build
options: LM Studio, TensorFold, llama.cpp, vLLM and others
what_it_changes: Speed, which models load at all
effect: Same Qwen3.8 27B 4-bit build: 16.7 tok/s in LM Studio, 15.2 in TensorFold (10% apart), same score. Several MoE models were not served by one of the two runtimes

what_it_changes: Which runtime and hardware can use it; speed
